primitives.name: 2026 - The Traveling Tournament Problem An Overview - Bulck et al Operator 1
primitives.verbatim_quote: The TTP, formally introduced in the seminal paper of Easton et al.
primitives.latex: Minimize Total Travel Distance = \sum_{t \in Teams} \sum_{(i,j) \in Games_t} dist(i,j)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'dist(i,j)': 'Euclidean distance between venues i and j in kilometers', 'Teams': 'Set of all participating teams', 'Games_t': 'Ordered pairs of venues representing away games for team t'}
primitives.assumptions: Double round-robin structure, symmetric travel costs, no capacity constraints on venues.
primitives.breakdown_regime: NP-hard for large numbers of teams; optimal solutions become computationally intractable.

layer2.mapping: GSE State-Transition Mapping: Each game corresponds to a state transition with travel cost.
layer2.telemetry: Total kilometers traveled per season, measured empirically.

primitives.verbatim_quote: The TTP, formally introduced in the seminal paper of Easton et al.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H_t': 'Number of consecutive home games for team t', 'A_t': 'Number of consecutive away games for team t'}
primitives.assumptions: Teams prefer rest days after long road trips; prevents fatigue accumulation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violating this constraint leads to player burnout and poor performance.

layer2.mapping: GSI Conformal Inference: Models the uncertainty in travel fatigue effects across different team rosters.
layer2.telemetry: Player injury rates and performance metrics during extended road trips.

primitives.name: 2026 - The Traveling Tournament Problem An Overview - Bulck et al Operator 3
primitives.verbatim_quote: The TTP, formally introduced in the seminal paper of Easton et al.
primitives.latex: N(t) = \{timetable | timetables differ by a small set of swaps\}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N(t)': 'Neighborhood of timetable t', 'Swap': 'Exchange of two away games between teams'}
primitives.assumptions: Local optimality implies global optimality within the neighborhood structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Stuck in local minima when the solution space has many disconnected basins.

layer2.mapping: GSE Situational Reasoning: Evaluates multiple candidate timetables (situations) based on travel cost.
layer2.telemetry: Average number of iterations before convergence to a feasible schedule.

primitives.verbatim_quote: We review the principal problem variants and benchmark instances, and summarize the current state of the art in lower bounds, approximation guarantees, and exact and heuristic optimization algorithms.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'LB': 'Lower bound on total travel distance', 'min(dist(i,j))': 'Minimum pairwise distance between any two venues'}
primitives.assumptions: Complete bipartite graph; each venue pair contributes at least once to the tour.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Underestimates actual travel when venues are clustered geographically.

The TTP is a combinatorial optimization challenge that maps directly to state-transition systems in GSE and conformal prediction frameworks in GSI. The core issue is balancing immediate travel efficiency against long-term roster health. Metaheuristic approaches like simulated annealing exploit local optima but risk getting trapped in suboptimal regions. Exact methods provide theoretical guarantees but scale poorly with league size. The road trip constraint acts as a regularization term preventing overfitting to short-term travel minimization. Lower bounds serve as empirical Bayes priors, guiding search towards feasible schedules while maintaining diversity.
